comment:
Emit seeds/stress_aperture.json -- STRESS COMPRESSES APERTURE.

`arousal_window_coreg` narrows the WINDOW OF TOLERANCE under dysregulation. This
narrows a second thing on a different axis: WHAT THE AGENT CAN RESOLVE.

The two are not the same limitation. A narrow window is about how much arousal you
can carry before dysregulating. A narrow aperture is about which dimensions you can
assess at all -- and `future_manifold.rs` counts an unresolved dimension as
UNASSESSED (`information_loss`), never as failed (`loss`). So a dysregulated agent
becomes measurably STUPID in the technical sense: not wrong, unable to tell.

Which dimensions survive is READ FROM GRAPH DATA (`AffectiveState.stress_resolves`),
exactly as `observer_aperture` reads `Observer.resolves`. A hand-tuned "stress
factor" would be the scalar-standing-in-for-a-shape defect `CLAUDE.md` names, and
would make the result unfalsifiable by construction.

Prereg: STRESS_COMPRESSES_APERTURE_PREREG.md (block 366000).

rules.name: sa_compress_on_dysregulation
rules.comment: A dysregulated affective state narrows what its projection policy can resolve. The mask is the state's own `stress_resolves` -- graph data, not a tuned coefficient -- so an agent whose stress spares a dimension keeps it, and the fixture cannot smuggle in the answer as a magnitude. Guarded on the current value so the fixpoint terminates.

rules.name: sa_restore_on_regulation
rules.comment: Returning to the window restores the full aperture. The recovery is the point: without it 'nothing helps a stressed agent' would pass trivially for an agent that is simply broken, and the registered crossover would have no positive control.
